A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AnyMAC and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, Appendix A, and supplementary case illustrations. The material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original AnyMAC benchmark results, component ablations, malicious-agent robustness tests, and qualitative routing examples.

after.justification: v2 retains original AnyMAC benchmark results, ablations, robustness tests, and routing examples, including the appendix illustrations.

M1.justification: The transformer router, next-agent prediction, next-context selection, RL objective, and efficiency variant remain unchanged. Expanded notation and prompt descriptions do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both evaluate MMLU, GSM8K, MultiArith, SVAMP, AQuA, and HumanEval. The malicious-agent scenario and qualitative example coverage are also retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 removes ComplexCoT, SC (CoT), and SC (Complex). The other comparators remain, while Section 5.1 still lists ComplexCoT and self-consistency among the baselines.

E3.justification: The reported splits, question-selection rules, models, temperatures, agent limit, evaluation metrics, and budgets of 80 questions and 1,000 training trajectories per dataset remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the malicious-agent experiment in Figure 3, the three component ablations in Table 2, and the routing case studies in Figures 5–6. Their analytical questions and evidence are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Appendix A's reward normalization remains unchanged training machinery.

E6.justification: v2 removes the six-dataset scores and averages for ComplexCoT and both self-consistency variants from Table 1. Retained scores and graphical findings are unchanged, including AnyMAC's 90.62% average accuracy and the Table 2 ablation results.

T1.justification: No substantive mathematical or proof changes appear. Appendix A.2 splits v1's normalization equation into Equations 24–25 without changing its mathematics; added notation explanations introduce no formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about sequential coordination, a broader topology space, adaptive context access, and accuracy–efficiency advantages.

C2.justification: The interpretations of adaptive routing, adversarial resilience, and accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs remain unchanged. Section 7 retains the same limitations concerning long contexts, limited RL training data, and costly scaling.

D1.justification: Section 3 now explicitly includes Base_t and Tool_t in the system-prompt description alongside role and state. This expands documentation of already-defined agent components; other implementation settings, appendix training details, and code-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Sections 1–2 add citations and briefly expand coverage of external-knowledge in-context learning, trustworthiness, and explainability. The taxonomy of collaboration methods and positioning against graph-based approaches remain intact.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized related-work additions, clarifies history indices and contextualized-token notation, and standardizes several method names, including AnyMAC-ACC to AnyMAC in captions. The overall organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 is shortened by three rows, captions update method names, and Appendix A.2 displays reward normalization across two equations. Typography and text reflow change modestly; all six figures retain their substantive visual content.

improvement.justification: Notation explanations and related-work context improve modestly, but Table 1 loses three comparator rows while Section 5.1 continues to claim those comparisons. This introduces a reporting inconsistency and reduces comparison completeness. The retained results and main scientific support are unchanged, so the overall decline is limited.
